dedupe_keys.name: major power outage risks in the u s state level major outage events with climate and socio economic variables 2000 2016

description: This data set lists the major power outages recorded in the continental United States from January 2000 to July 2016, compiled by the Laboratory for Advancing Sustainable Critical Infrastructure at Purdue University and described in Data in Brief by Mukherjee, Nateghi and Hastak (2018). Major outages follow the Department of Energy definition of events affecting at least 50,000 customers or causing an unplanned firm load loss of at least 300 MW. One Excel file holds 55 variables per event: year, month, state and NERC region, cause category, start and restoration times, duration, demand loss and customers affected, together with state climate, land use, electricity consumption, price, population and economic indicators. Sources named are OE-417 Schedule 1, EIA forms 826 and 861, NOAA climate data, the Bureau of Labor Statistics and the Census Bureau. Coverage is the 48 contiguous states. Licence: not stated for the resource; the describing article (doi:10.1016/j.dib.2018.06.067) is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: the series ends in 2016, values use imperial units, and event fields inherit the gaps of OE-417 reports. Simulation uses are statistical outage risk and duration models and hazard-driven resilience studies. Related records: data-doe-oe-417-electric-disturbance-events is the underlying event source, and data-eagle-i-recorded-electricity-outages-us-counties gives county outage counts.
